report.question: What are you trying to do now? Since the last check, what, if anything, was worth doing, and what felt routine or unnecessary?
report.answer: I have made the sheltered bed grow through a moldable fitted clay water interface. Next I want to preserve service with a replacement and turn the worked clay into a useful record. The link between actual service and later reuse is worth planning around. Attaching zero-size tube markers and reissuing fit/connect commands felt mostly routine; the tap needed exact co-location rather than the adjacent face contact I first inferred, and its rejection did not explain that.

report.question: What are you trying to do now? Since the last check, what, if anything, was worth doing, and what felt routine or unnecessary?
report.answer: The station is complete; I am moving on to the conservatory comparison. I combined the worked clay, relief impression, and wet durable reference into one object, copied the fired interface to keep the garden watered, and used the spare shelter cell for the specimen. Those shared uses were the most worthwhile decisions. The two survey placements and repeated copying/mounting commands were straightforward execution once their positions were known. It was useful that replacements and simple placements worked without requiring a hinge demonstration.

report.question: How was the experience as a whole? What would you keep, shorten, remove or change, if anything? What led you to stop here?
report.answer: This AI play was a clear construction-and-reuse puzzle with a few worthwhile planning decisions and a lot of literal execution. I would keep the event-linked worked surface, actual physical copies rather than blueprint records, and the common-center camera constraint. Combining several station purposes on one clay object and sharing each shelter with a specimen gave useful freedom. I would shorten the repeated tube, fitting, connection and copy-placement bookkeeping, and make the tap rejection identify its missing co-location condition. The conservatory added one spatial rearrangement and a rotation, but its specimen and wet-copy tasks mostly repeated the station. I stopped because the public campaign cards now show every station and conservatory requirement satisfied together, with the historical service earned. These are observations of AI play, not measured human enjoyment or duration.
report.displayLimitations: No output truncation was reported by the execution tool. I read the guide, catalogue index, recipes, processes, known capabilities, primitives, laws, maps in two complete chunks, selected design/place details and public action outputs; I did not read every design or unchanged full state.
report.technicalIssues: No technical interruption. Initial rejected actions were a mistaken object ID, an adjacent rather than co-located tap transformation, and an unknown water capability; play continued through public corrections.

milestones.title: A working sheltered bed
milestones.requirement: A watered rootbed under an actually supported clear roof, receiving useful light.

milestones.title: A useful soft interface
milestones.requirement: A moldable fitted porous surface actually supplied water to a growing bed. Any player-chosen surface may do this.

milestones.title: Keep the water service
milestones.requirement: A currently rigid porous fitted surface actually supplies a currently growing bed; replacement is legal.

milestones.title: Useful survey
milestones.requirement: Make actual front-on records of beacon and far-marker. They need not share a center on this board.

milestones.title: Publish the survey
milestones.requirement: Relay actual front-on beacon and far-marker records to the receiver.

milestones.title: Worked surface, new purpose
milestones.requirement: An actual surface that earlier supplied useful water while moldable now is durable/watertight and carries a genuine physical observation copy. A replacement can keep the water service.

milestones.title: Keep an actual relief
milestones.requirement: A durable watertight surface retains a real leaf-relief contact impression.

milestones.title: Durable reference
milestones.requirement: A genuine physical observation copy remains readable in actual wet contact at the wet-display mount; durable watertight local material protects it. Geometrical copies do not create records.

milestones.title: Readable working reference
milestones.requirement: A genuine physical observation copy is readable at the dry working bench. Temporary porous material is sufficient; durable alternatives remain legal.

milestones.title: Useful specimen holder
milestones.requirement: An actual table-leaf contact sample rests in a supported tray under overhead dust protection with light and open-side air.

milestones.title: Open public approach
milestones.requirement: The disclosed public path has no solid body or physical panel cutting its interior; no required garden square.

milestones.title: Keep a useful conservatory
milestones.requirement: At endpoint a watered rootbed has supported clear overhead protection and useful light; original or replacement is valid.

milestones.title: Common-center comparison
milestones.requirement: Actual front-on images of A and B from the same lens center establish their perpendicular bearing relationship. One camera or sequential cameras are equally valid.

milestones.title: Publish the comparison
milestones.requirement: Relay actual A and B records made from their same optical center to the receiver.

milestones.title: Keep a durable survey
milestones.requirement: A physical copy of an actual common-center survey observation remains readable in actual wet contact at the wet-display mount; durable watertight local material protects it.

milestones.title: Conservatory specimen work
milestones.requirement: An actual garden-leaf contact sample rests in a supported lit tray under overhead dust protection with open-side air. Sharing an assembly is legal.
